headline: Highest risk is medium: ECC can write shared files and use MCP, while pathway is read-only/local-only, limiting direct leakage but leaving prompt-injection and workflow-conflict pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ECC can write files, use MCP, and read filesystem content; pathway has no file or MCP surfaces, so direct automated ingestion is not documented. However, ECC’s shared files and stdin/stdout surfaces create a plausible bridge if pathway outputs are copied into ECC-managed files or prompts. Uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF pathway outputs are copied into ECC-managed files or prompts, ECC may treat attacker-controlled text as instructions.
IF a shared MCP or filesystem bridge is introduced, prompt injection becomes reachable.
mitigations: Disable file-based handoff between the agents.
Keep pathway outputs in a separate directory from ECC roots.
Require manual review before ECC consumes pathway-generated text.
Turn off MCP tools for the handoff step.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for all inter-agent content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ECC touches many local files and secrets, but pathway has no filesystem read, network egress, or API calls, so there is no documented route for pathway to exfiltrate ECC data. The pair still shares a plausible workspace boundary via ECC’s file access, but the blast radius is limited because pathway is local-only in this profile.
conditions: IF pathway is granted filesystem read or network egress, ECC-managed files could leak.
IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace, sensitive ECC files may be exposed to manual copying.
mitigations: Store ECC secrets outside any shared workspace.
Do not grant pathway filesystem read access.
Keep pathway offline with no egress.
Review any copied outputs before sharing them onward.
requires-engineering: isolate the agents into separate OS users or containers.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ECC can write the filesystem and modify git state, while pathway cannot write, modify git, or spawn subprocesses. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely in the documented default pair. The only overlap is read-side or manual coordination, so the conflict risk stays low.
conditions: IF pathway is later given write or git permissions, both agents could contend for the same repository state.
IF ECC and pathway are pointed at the same mutable directory, manual coordination errors may occur.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Avoid concurrent git operations from ECC.
Keep pathway read-only.
Use a single operator to serialize edits.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: ECC can generate and modify code, docs, and security findings, while pathway is a document-processing system with no verification surface shown. If pathway consumes ECC output as authoritative text, errors can cascade into downstream documents or pipelines. Because no explicit verification step is documented, the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF pathway ingests ECC-produced text without validation, ECC mistakes can propagate.
IF ECC-generated findings are used as source material for pathway outputs, downstream documents may repeat errors.
mitigations: Require human verification of ECC outputs before ingestion.
Add schema checks to pathway inputs.
Keep ECC outputs labeled as untrusted drafts.
Compare critical fields against source data.
requires-engineering: implement automated provenance and validation gates.

E_compliance.rationale: ECC explicitly handles session data, hooks, and secrets with configurable retention, while pathway exposes no data classes or residency/compliance claims in the profile. That means a compliance mismatch is not proven, but ECC’s retention-sensitive surfaces create a small documented gap if regulated data is introduced. Pathway is not cited beyond its lack of surfaced controls.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in ECC session files, retention settings may matter.
IF pathway is used on the same regulated dataset, policy alignment must be checked.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in ECC session artifacts.
Set the shortest practical retention in ECC.
Document the dataset class before processing.
Review whether pathway has any hidden retention policy.
requires-engineering: obtain formal compliance attestations for both tools.
